title: Spring-cage feed-through terminal block, 2.5 mm² class, grey

sources.citation: real-world (product class): 2.5 mm² spring-cage feed-through blocks are 5.1–5.2 mm wide, about 48.5–59.5 mm long and 36.5–38.5 mm high (makers’ datasheets, read 2026-11-12). Drawn 5 × 56 × 36 mm: the width rounded down to whole mm, the length inside the band, the height 0.5 mm under it (rounded to whole mm).
game-design: two spring cages, top (1) and bottom (2), 26 mm off the rail; conductors enter the top and bottom faces. Not taken from a product drawing.

game-design: clips onto a 35 mm top-hat rail (IEC 60715, cited by number), 5 mm along it, centred on the rail: its origin sits 45 − 28 = 17 mm above the mount origin (DIN 43880’s 90 mm modular-device line, ADR 0015 note 7).

real-world (product class): the 2.5 mm² spring-cage class takes 26/28–12 AWG copper (of which 22–12 is used here; UL/CSA 20 A, 600 V), solid or stranded, stranded in a ferrule, with an 8–10 mm strip (makers’ datasheets, read 2026-11-12); one conductor per cage. A spring’s force is fixed, so no torque and no drive (the release slot’s blade is not modelled).
game-design: a 10 ± 1 mm strip (inside the class’s 8–10 mm), the spring-cage clamp type and a 9 mm cage depth.

game-design (ADR 0018 §4.1, §3.3): R₀ 0.3 mΩ, the ADR’s spring-cage example inside NBS BSS 128’s (1980) 1.5 mΩ assembly acceptance limit. A terminal-block voltage-drop acceptance (at most 3.2 mV per block, two clamps, at a DC test current of 0.1 × the rated section’s current) gives at most 1.33 mΩ per block at 2.5 mm² (2.4 A); the model’s two clamps at 0.3 mΩ (0.6 mΩ, plus the ideal bridge) sit inside it. Read on a maker’s terminal-block test page (read 2026-11-12: https://www.phoenixcontact.com/en-ch/quality-tests-for-terminal-blocks/electrical-tests-terminal-blocks), which attributes the test to IEC 60947-7-1, IEC 61984 and UL 1059 (cited by number only; the standards themselves unverified). The heat path, 0.02 W/K, is a game-design scaling below the screw class’s calibrated 0.026 W/K for a smaller clamp (no derivation); the heat capacity, 0.35 J/K, is about 0.8 g of spring steel (about 460–490 J/(kg·K)) and a copper bar (about 385 J/(kg·K)).
